Definition: from G1909 and potheo (to yearn); to dote upon, i.e. intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully):--(earnestly) desire (greatly), (greatly) long (after), lust.
BiblicalUsage: Epipotheo means to long for, to yearn intensely — to dote upon with lawful desire. Paul longs to see the Romans that he may impart a spiritual gift; we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house from heaven; God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ; and as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.
TheologicalSignificance: A heart that longs for nothing is a heart that is not alive, and the newborn, the apostle, and the saint all prove it. I believe longing is the mark of life: milk for the newborn, brethren for the apostle, heaven for the saint.
